doc.title: Karolina Strassmayer interviewed by Monk Rowe, May 25, 2023

title: Miles Davis Kind of Blue on the train to school
summary: A friend's dumped cassette of Kind of Blue on the early commute changed her life; her grandfather identified it as jazz and she bought a saxophone with her moped money.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: to our school which was about an hour away. And one morning my friend came with a bag of cassette tapes. I mean we’re talking about the 80s right, so we’re still dealing with cassette tapes. And her older sister had — she wanted to get rid of some of those tapes and just dumped them on her little sister who was my friend and then she came to the train station in the morning with this bag and she said, “Oh my sister gave me these tapes and I checked it out but it’s horrible, I don’t know what it is but I don’t like it.” So she just basically dumped this bag into my lap and I thought okay we’re going to be on the train, I have my Walkman with me, why not? So I just grabbed one of the tapes and it said “Miles Davis Kind of Blue.” I had no idea who Miles Davis was, I had no idea what “Kind of Blue” was, I just was completely naïve and didn’t know anything about that. And I put in the cassette tape, the train started moving, it was still dark outside, it was wintertime, and I pressed play and the first thing I heard it just blew my mind — it just blew me away — I had no idea what I was hearing but I knew that it was such a raw power and energy to it and I knew this is what I have to do. I have to do this. But I didn’t even know what instrument it was. So I went with this tape to my grandfather and he listened to it for a few minutes you know because he was a hobby musician and conductor I thought he would be able to tell me what it was. And he listened to it and after a couple of minutes he said, “You know I think this might be jazz.” You know? So little by little I found out more and more until eventually I found out what I heard was Julian “Cannonball” Adderley on the alto saxophone. And then basically I sold my Moped and bought a saxophone for it and yep, that was really the trajectory of my life was set at that moment. And I’m grateful for that.
